To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) in the target fragmentation rapidity region all three models predict the same scaling properties of proton cross sections, (2) the transition layer is the source of protons in this region and (3) the transition layer formation is due to mutual transparency.

in the central rapidities region, especially in the central collisions of identical ions, considerable differences are observed in the predictions of three models, and the experimental study of the transition layer is required.
the scaling properties of the spectra of protons produced in high energy heavy ion collisions are due to the emission from the transition layer formed on the boundary of overlapping nuclei.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of space-time evolution of the nuclear system created in relativistic nucleus-nuclear collisions.

the study of the space-time structure of high-energy heavy ion collisions, with the analysis of the role of the transition layer in the formation of the inclusive cross sections and with a search for the scaling laws of inclusive spectra.
the study of the space-time picture of high energy heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are not sufficient to discriminate between the models.
the models of relativistic heavy ion collisions have been developed to a level where it becomes possible to perform a quantitative analysis of experimental data.

, in spite of the fact that the experimental data on proton spectra in high-energy heavy-ion reactions are rather scarce, their analysis allows us to draw a number of important conclusions concerning the nature of the processes of particle emission and to make a number of predictions for future experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, at present, we are not able to distinguish between different models of high-energy heavy ion collisions.
the scaling of proton spectra is not a unique feature of the hydrodynamial model and is rather a property of the transition layer.
, at least at the energies considered, the scaling properties of inclusive proton spectra are well reproduced by the intranuclear-cascade and hydrodynamical models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transition layer is a crucial part of the collision dynamics.
the proton spectra in high energy heavy-ion collisions are sensitive probes to the properties of the transition region between the projectile and target nuclei.
the scaling properties of high-energy heavy ion collisions are not universal and depend on the collision system.
